title: The い-stem: the great connector
summary: The い-stem is the verb's connecting form: it takes ます, helper adjectives like やすい, compounds, joins clauses and makes a noun.

blocks.text: Take a verb's う-row ending and shift it to the い-row (読む → 読み, 食べる → 食べ). That is the **い-stem**, the "connective use form" (連用形). The course calls it **the great connector**, because it does so many different joining jobs. It is not the "base form": ます is just one helper attached to it.
It takes **ます**, plenty of dedicated helper adjectives and nouns, and it joins verbs into compounds, much as the て-form does.

rows: 読みやすい (easy to read), 読みにくい
読み始める, 読み込む
店に行き、パンを買った
休む → 休み, 読む → 読み

blocks.en: This book is easy to read.

blocks.jp: 歩きながらスマホを見ないでください。
blocks.en: Please don't look at your phone while walking.

blocks.jp: 店に行き、パンを買った。
blocks.en: I went to the store and bought bread.

blocks.text: The い-stem can also join with a noun to make a new noun: 泣き + 虫 = 泣き虫 (a crybaby), 読み + 方 = 読み方 (way of reading). A compound takes on the character of its last element, so 読み込み中 is a noun.

items: い-stem = う-ending shifted to the い-row (読む → 読み).
It connects ます, やすい / にくい, ながら, そう, and compounds.
It can join two clauses like the て-form: 行き、買った.
It is also the **noun form** of a verb: 休む → 休み.
